title: [GOAL] Strong learned pipeline to ~0.9 (proper detector + motion linker), no toy/stopgap
description:
MINDSET: build the REAL thing, no 'simple baseline first / graduate later' — that trap wasted this session on a width-16 toy. Target the pack (~0.9 = pilkwang learned tier). NO CPU-only constraint, GPU/offline-wheels fine.

REALIZATION: score = edge Jaccard. Public classical 0.427->0.857 is almost ALL linker (two-pass motion Hungarian + gap-close); learned pack ~0.897 = proper TemporalUNet3D detector + edge transformer + ILP. We spent this session on the DETECTOR half at width-16 and left the LINKER at nearest-neighbour. BOTH halves are toys.

SPINE (learned path is primary):
1. PROPER learned detector — width 64+, anti-saturation bg-crops (detector saturates: fires >0.99 on 28% of voxels at 12k = blobs not cells; kills sparse 44b6 to 0.000), weight-decay, EARLY-STOP+checkpoints (steps non-monotonic: 8k peak 0.472, 12k/16k collapse). NOT the width-16 toy. [o46 c5d m0h ns3 5ns]
2. STRONG linker — motion-predicted two-pass Hungarian + gap-close [zzn]; ILP available [ilp_linking]. Feeds from EITHER detector. Building it lifts every path.
3. Metric trust — verify local<->LB (pending 8k 55146849 + classical calibration) [387]. Nothing above matters until local score predicts LB.
4. Compose best detector + best linker + post-proc, eval fold-0, submit, iterate to 0.9.

KEEP ALL existing methods as swappable alternatives (NN/ILP/Division linkers, DoG + learned detectors) — additive via Linker Protocol + GraphTransform chain, nothing deleted.

title: Disk response cache: forward each detector once, sweep readouts instantly
description: Forward every fold-0 val frame ONCE per detector checkpoint, save the per-frame probability volumes (fp16) to disk keyed by (checkpoint, video). Then threshold/keep-N/linker/short-track/linefit experiments read cached responses -> instant, no re-forward. Rebuild only after a retrain. Makes the qc5 + linker + post-proc iteration seconds instead of 148s/video. Part of goal dlf.
close_reason: fp16+channels_last forward (148->15s/video), ResponseCache (replay 0.7s), extract-once sweep (Tx11->1x11s). Commit febd89f. Root-caused bf16-NMS interaction (bf16 quantizes response -> false plateaus -> under-detection; fp16 correct).

title: [GOAL] Sub-5-minute detector keep/kill loop (fast + correct eval)
description:
PREMISE: speed of the EVAL loop is king — training is already fast (2x rechunk, 29min, GPU 86-96%). The tax is inference: 148s/video full-frame forward gates every detector keep/kill (fold-0 subset ~15min, full ~1.6h). Make a detector idea -> fold-0 score take <5 min. THREE parts:
1. CORRECTNESS FIRST (qc5): plateau-NMS fix. Without it evals are WRONG (100k plateau nodes) AND slow (linker cdist 246s / OOM). One fix buys both correctness and speed.
2. INFERENCE SPEED (d2u): channels_last_3d + torch.compile + batched-timepoint forward. Target 148s -> <60s/video, no accuracy change, GPU-bound.
3. RESPONSE CACHE: forward each detector ONCE, cache the per-frame probability volumes to disk; then every threshold/keep-N/linker/post-proc experiment is INSTANT (no re-forward). Rebuild the fold-0 cache after a retrain only.
OUTCOME: detector idea -> cached forward (once, ~fast) -> sweep readouts/linkers/postproc in seconds -> trustworthy fold-0 number in minutes. Unblocks the detector-quality epic 7bx (bg-crops-no-smoothing, density sampling) with a tight loop.

title: Fix plateau NMS in peaks.py (max-pool marks every voxel of a flat blob)
description: peaks._local_maxima uses volume==maxpool(volume): on a SATURATED detector the response is flat plateaus at prob~1, so EVERY voxel of a plateau equals the neighbourhood max -> ~1e5 'peaks'/frame (measured 100476/frame on aug@0.99, 528k/163k on above_threshold evals). This (a) exploded the linker cdist to OOM (the machine-killer), (b) POLLUTED every detector comparison this session (bg-crops '0.06', calibration 'refuted', 528k/163k counts are plateau artifacts NOT real detections). Fix: collapse each connected plateau to ONE centre (connected-component label -> max-value voxel per component, e.g. scipy.ndimage.maximum_position on the is_peak mask). Then above_threshold gives real cell counts, keep-N localises properly, and detector evals become TRUSTWORTHY. HIGHEST priority - blocks all detector-quality work (7bx). After fix: re-eval aug vs bg-crops-no-smoothing correctly.
close_reason: connected-component plateau collapse committed; test_above_threshold_collapses_a_plateau_to_one_centre green

title: Kaggle notebook submission (competition is notebook-only)
description: Competition biohub-cell-tracking-during-development REJECTS file-CSV submissions: 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION 'only accepts Submissions from Notebooks'. Must submit via a Kaggle notebook. Steps: (1) package model weights (detector_bce_aug.pt etc) + celltrack/core code as a Kaggle dataset (offline, no internet), (2) notebook imports it, runs the pipeline (memory-safe batched forward -> peaks.centres keep-N -> NN linker -> ShortTrackFilter -> LinefitSmoother -> Submission.write_csv) on root.videos('test'), (3) verify offline deps present in Kaggle image (torch/numpy/scipy/polars/zarr; NO motile/SCIP). Local submission.csv already builds correctly (scratchpad/build_submission.py, keep250/frame, 24s/video, RAM flat) - only the upload mechanism blocks. CRITICAL: use keep-N not above_threshold (saturated detector -> 100k plateau nodes/frame -> linker cdist 100k^2 -> OOM).
close_reason: learned kernel submitted on T4 (celltrack-learned-submit v4), scoring. kaggle/ folder + README document the notebook-only path.

title: Epic: training data-pipeline speedup — saturate the GPU
description: GOAL: kill the training data bottleneck so a full detector run finishes in ~10-15min (not ~50min) and the GPU runs >90% util (not 77% oscillating). ROOT CAUSE (measured): frames are (100,64,256,256) uint16 chunked one-timepoint-per-chunk = 8MB/read; a 16x64x64 crop needs 0.26MB, so we decompress 32x too much; the DataLoader (55 crops/s, 8 workers) cannot keep the forward fed. PLAN (code in parallel to the running w64 job, then RESTART training on the fast pipeline): (1) 6v0 re-chunk - build tools/rechunk.py: read each train+test video '0' array, rewrite to a NEW store (processed/rechunked/<name>.zarr or a .rechunked sibling) with small 3D chunks e.g. (1,32,64,64), preserving OME metadata; wire CellVideo/run.py to read the re-chunked store (a --rechunked flag or auto-detect). Expect ~32x less decompress -> workers saturate GPU. Non-destructive (keep originals). ~126GB rewrite, ~20-40min one-time. (2) aec bump --workers 8->16 (32 threads). DONE-WHEN: a width-64 batch-16 run holds >90% GPU util and finishes 12k steps in <15min; fold-0 eval pipeline still runs (aug detector->NN->short-track->linefit). Consider ogy (RAM cache) / 5vh (Rust) only if still data-bound after re-chunk. Test: rechunk a tiny fixture video, assert same data + smaller chunks; integration: CellVideo reads re-chunked store identically.
close_reason: epic done: data bottleneck removed, GPU saturated. see 6v0/aec.

title: Calibration measurement — probability histogram + reliability
description: Log the predicted-probability histogram on held-out crops. A well-calibrated detector spreads probabilities and separates at ~0.5; ours bunches at 1.0. Track this metric across experiments.
notes: Use Gini (2*AUC-1) for discrimination (does the detector rank cell-voxels above background) alongside the probability histogram for spread/calibration. Owner: gini ok where applicable.

title: Epic: detector quality — fix calibration/overfit, climb detector-side score
description: Detector is now the bottleneck (linker=ILP, post-proc=short-track+linefit all done; pooled 0.707 fold-0 but LEAKY). Symptoms: (a) overfit - loss->0.002 on 4 videos, (b) overconfident/poorly calibrated - operating threshold 0.99 not ~0.5, probabilities bunched near 1.0. ROOT: trained on 4/199 videos. This epic: train on real data scale + regularize + calibrate, measure detector-side and end-to-end fold-0 gains. Each experiment = retrain -> rebuild cache -> eval pipeline (aug detector -> ILP -> short-track -> linefit).
notes: Next run config: --width 64 --batch 16 (2x from 8; util ~50% at batch 8, memory only 7/31.5GB, 2x should saturate without wasting VRAM) --label-smoothing 0.05 (intensity aug now automatic). --videos 0 fold-aware (158 videos). More steps for real epochs.

title: Re-chunk training data to crop-sized zarr chunks (throughput)
description: Measured: GPU 0-1% during training, 43 crops/s, data-bound. Root cause = zarr chunked one-timepoint-per-chunk, so each small crop decompresses a full ~100MB timepoint volume. Frame LRU cache won't help (random anchors across videos = cache misses). Proper fix: offline re-chunk the processed zarr into small 3D chunks (e.g. 16x64x64-ish) so a crop reads only its region. Only worth it if training throughput becomes the constraint (currently 3000 steps/9min is fine; score is the goal). Under epic 02x.
notes: CONCRETE: frames are (100,64,256,256) uint16, chunked (1,64,256,256) = 8MB/timepoint. A 16x64x64 crop needs 0.26MB -> we decompress 32x too much per read. THIS is the training data bottleneck (77% GPU util, oscillating; loader can't keep forward fed at 55 crops/s). FIX: rewrite '0' array chunks to small 3D blocks e.g. (1,32,64,64) so a crop reads ~1 chunk not a whole plane -> ~32x less decompress -> workers saturate GPU. Non-destructive: write re-chunked copies to processed/rechunked/, wire CellVideo/run to read them. Cost: ~126GB rewrite (158 videos x 800MB), ~20-40min. RAM=94GB (full dataset 126GB doesn't fit, so re-chunk beats RAM-cache). PRIORITY - recurring bottleneck. P0.
close_reason: windowed reads + (1,16,128,128) rechunk: GPU 3%->86-96%, 3.3->7.5 steps/s (2.2x). committed ff4e0e0.

title: Post-proc GraphTransform chain: short-track filter, gap-close, linefit smooth
description: NB3's 0.63->0.857 came largely from post-processing. Composable GraphTransform strategies applied to a linked TrackGraph: (1) filter_short_track_components (drop weakly-connected comps < min_len ~7 unless they contain a division) - highest impact, (2) close_single_frame_gaps (end at t -> start at t+2 within ~6um, reuse isolated node else synth midpoint), (3) linefit_smooth (topology-preserving coord smoothing on linear interiors, w~0.8, lifts 7um match rate). Each scored for marginal gain on cached detections. Under epic 02x.
close_reason: implemented + landed (short_track/linefit, detection cache, eval_pipeline harness, classification_loss, dog_detection, ilp_linking) — learned pipeline works end-to-end, submitted.

title: Cache detections for fast linker/post-proc iteration
description: Every fold-0 experiment re-forwards the whole video (~30s) even when only the linker/post-proc changes (detections fixed). Cache per-frame centres per (checkpoint, threshold) to disk once; eval loads cache + links+scores in ~2-3s (15x faster iteration). Enables rapid post-proc/operating-point tuning. Under epic 02x.
close_reason: implemented + landed (short_track/linefit, detection cache, eval_pipeline harness, classification_loss, dog_detection, ilp_linking) — learned pipeline works end-to-end, submitted.

title: Assemble learned pipeline + composable fold-0 scoring harness
description: Wire best Detector + best Linker + post-proc chain into one scored pipeline. Composable harness: swap any strategy, score end-to-end on fold 0 with core/metrics/ SplitScore, report marginal contribution of each piece. Replaces scratch eval_dog.py as a committed CLI. Blocks 02x.
close_reason: implemented + landed (short_track/linefit, detection cache, eval_pipeline harness, classification_loss, dog_detection, ilp_linking) — learned pipeline works end-to-end, submitted.

title: ILP graph linker (motile/tracksdata + SCIP), division-aware, CPU-parallel per video
description: Winning linker family = ILP min-cost graph selection. Use motile or tracksdata with open SCIP (pyscipopt) solver (Gurobi unlicensable in kernel). Costs: edge reward=-edge_prob, appearance/disappearance~0.1, division_weight~1.0. Division-aware (out-degree up to 2). Run per-video, parallel across videos on 16c/32t CPU. Linker Protocol sibling. Blocks 02x.
close_reason: implemented + landed (short_track/linefit, detection cache, eval_pipeline harness, classification_loss, dog_detection, ilp_linking) — learned pipeline works end-to-end, submitted.

title: Detector: class-balanced BCE-with-logits + high-threshold (~0.99) prob local-maxima inference
description: THE win lever (0.73->0.897 is all detection). Swap MaskedDetectionLoss (MSE heatmap) for masked class-balanced BCE-with-logits: positives=GT centre voxels weight 1/N+, negatives weight alpha/N- with alpha~0.01, keep the unknown-region mask. Inference: detections = local maxima of sigmoid(logit) above prob threshold ~0.99 (PeakExtractor variant with absolute threshold). High precision -> stable centres (fixes jitter) + low count -> node-count bonus. Retrain DetectionUNet on RTX5090. Blocks 02x.
close_reason: implemented + landed (short_track/linefit, detection cache, eval_pipeline harness, classification_loss, dog_detection, ilp_linking) — learned pipeline works end-to-end, submitted.

title: Motion-predicted two-pass Hungarian linker (tight 6um / loose 10um, half-velocity)
description: NB3/NB4 linker: two-pass linear_sum_assignment, pass1 tight gate ~6um, pass2 loose ~10um on leftovers, cost = distance to half-velocity-predicted position, gate on raw displacement. Plus close_single_frame_gaps, filter_short_tracks(>=4 unless division), linefit_smooth (topology-preserving coord smoothing, w~0.8). Sibling to NearestNeighbourLinker. Blocks 02x.
close_reason: MotionHungarianLinker shipped (celltrack/motion_linking.py, 3 tests, gates pass)

title: DoG band-pass detector (NB3-style) + high-precision low-count operating point
description: Public NB3 (lb-0-857, no hacks) = multi-scale DoG band-pass + two-pass motion Hungarian + gap-close + short-track filter + linefit smooth, LB 0.857 CPU-only. Our LoG+NN = 0.427. Build DoGDetector (sibling to BlobDetector): multi-scale DoG (gaussian(sig_lo)-gaussian(sig_hi)), physical NMS, sub-voxel centroid refine, high-precision threshold. KEY: operate at high-precision LOW node count (well below N_total 23700) to farm the node-count bonus (adj = jaccard*(1-0.1*ratio), up to x1.1) WITHOUT losing annotated-lineage recall. Revises operating-point-sweep finding (1.0x was wrong for a precise detector). Tune count on fold-0 with core/metrics/. Blocks 02x.
close_reason: implemented + landed (short_track/linefit, detection cache, eval_pipeline harness, classification_loss, dog_detection, ilp_linking) — learned pipeline works end-to-end, submitted.

title: Epic: climb to top of leaderboard (pack at 0.92, we are 0.427)
description: Public LB: top 0.942, dense wall 0.92-0.94 (20+ teams). Our classical LoG+NN = 0.427. Public notebooks reveal the method stack: UNet+ILP tracking (v4-unet-ilp-reproduction), lb897-baseline (0.897), DoG band-pass detection (0.73), plus multiple 'metric-hack' notebooks (the 0.92 wall may be partly metric exploitation of the node-count adjustment term). Notebooks pulled to scratchpad/nb/.

title: Cell-density-stratified sampling (continuum 1-20 cells/frame)
description: Sampling is uniform-per-video (dataset.py:51), skewed 64/36 to 6bba by video count (71 44b6 / 128 6bba). Real difficulty axis is annotated cell DENSITY, a continuum 1-20 cells/frame (44b6 median 2.1, 6bba 8.4, overlapping) NOT the acquisition label. Bin videos/timepoints by cells/frame, sample bins evenly. Subsumes acquisition + temporal balance (density grows via divisions). Caveat: annotated density only (unlabeled cells invisible); uniform-density may diverge from eval mix -> keep/kill test. Justified by test being 2/prefix.
close_reason: Implemented DensitySampling (octave-uniform video draws, --density-stratified) + tested. REFUTED as a lever: subset 0.21 vs 8k-uniform 0.636, tanked both prefixes (over-weights rare sparse-density videos, starves positive gradient). Code kept, flag off by default. See memory density-stratify-refuted-2026-07-31. Commit df37299.

title: Inference/compute speed: torch.compile + channels_last_3d + temporal batching + bigger batch
description: Full-video forward is FLOP-bound: 148-159s/video (w64 3D U-Net over 64x256x256, GPU 99% at batch 1). Levers, no accuracy change: (1) batch timepoints (batch 2->3 already cut 159->148s in eval), (2) channels_last_3d memory format (big conv3d speedup on Blackwell), (3) torch.compile (20-40% fusion), (4) bigger TRAIN batch (mem 8.5/32GB -> more util). NOT gradient checkpointing (trades compute for memory, we are not memory-bound). Target: <60s/video inference, faster train epoch.
close_reason: fp16+channels_last forward (148->15s/video), ResponseCache (replay 0.7s), extract-once sweep (Tx11->1x11s). Commit febd89f. Root-caused bf16-NMS interaction (bf16 quantizes response -> false plateaus -> under-detection; fp16 correct).

title: Epoch-structured training: fixed random-crop batches/epoch + per-epoch val
description: Reframe the step-based loop into epochs (e.g. 500 steps=1 epoch) over the random-crop pool (already how CropDataset samples). Eval val each epoch with a FAST crop-based metric (BCE loss + detection recall on val-split crops, no backprop, seconds) — full-video tracking-score is 93s/video so can't run per-epoch. Log train+val per epoch to mlflow.

title: Background/random-negative crops to fix detector over-firing
description: Training crops are always anchored on an annotated cell (+jitter), so the model never sees large empty background. At full-frame inference it over-fires there: w64 detector emits 528k nodes at thr=0.5 on a 71-truth-node video, score 0.0, uncalibrated (needs 0.99+). Fix: sample a fraction of crops from uniformly-random locations (mostly empty tissue) so the model learns to be confidently-negative on background. The DetectionTarget mask still excludes ambiguous bright regions, so unannotated cells in a random crop carry no gradient (safe). Expected: calibrated detector operating near 0.5, far fewer false nodes to link (also speeds the linker). CropSampler gets background_fraction; run.py a flag; retrain w64 and re-eval on fold-0 val.

title: Quick win: bump DataLoader workers 8->16 (32 threads available)
description: Cheap partial fix for the data-bound training (frames 8MB, 55 crops/s at 8 workers). We have 16c/32t; --workers 16 doubles parallel decompress. Won't fully close the util gap (re-chunk 6v0 does) but immediate. Just a CLI value next run.
close_reason: windowed reads + (1,16,128,128) rechunk: GPU 3%->86-96%, 3.3->7.5 steps/s (2.2x). committed ff4e0e0.

title: Scale model width IF underfitting after more data
description: Only after overfit is cured by data+reg: if the detector underfits (train loss stops dropping, val plateaus low), increase width/depth. Bigger model is the UNDERFITTING fix, per owner. Guard against re-overfitting.

title: Regularization: weight decay + optional dropout
description: AdamW weight decay (and/or dropout in conv blocks) to fight overfit directly. Sweep a couple values, keep what helps fold-0.

title: Rotation augmentation (y-x isotropic plane)
description: Random 90-deg rotations in the isotropic y-x plane (coords rotated to match). More geometric variety; z left alone (anisotropic).

title: Label smoothing in the BCE objective — directly fix overconfidence
description: Targets 1->1-eps, 0->eps (eps~0.05) in MaskedBCEClassificationLoss so the model stops driving logits to saturation. Measure: does the operating threshold move toward 0.5 (better calibration) and does the score hold/improve?

title: Intensity augmentation (brightness/contrast jitter) in the crop sampler
description: Add per-crop intensity scale+offset jitter (clipped to [0,1]) to CropSampler alongside flips+anchor-jitter. Real test videos differ in intensity; variety improves generalization + calibration.

title: Train on full fold-train split (158 videos) — the real more-data fix
description: IN PROGRESS. Fold-aware (no leak), --videos 0 uses all 158 fold-0-train videos, 6000 steps. Expect overfit to break (loss should plateau higher) and calibration to improve. Get the CLEAN fold-0 number (no leakage). detector_bce_full.pt.

title: Lift sparse-video (44b6) score - the pooled drag
description: 44b6 (sparse acquisition) scores ~0.21-0.31 across ALL detectors (classical, MSE, aug BCE); 6bba (dense) hits 0.71. 44b6 caps the pooled. Investigate: is it the metric behaviour on sparse annotation, detection recall on 44b6, or linking? ILP already lifted it 0.213->0.305. Under epic 02x.

title: Operating-point sweep with ILP linker (per-video threshold)
description: Current best: aug BCE detector @0.99 + ILP = 0.671 pooled (44b6=0.305, 6bba=0.712). The 0.99 threshold gives 0.64x/0.97x gt; sweep thresholds WITH ILP + post-proc to find best operating point per acquisition (sparse 44b6 may prefer higher precision for the node-count bonus). Score all thresholds, not just closest-to-gt. Under epic 02x.

title: Deps + kernel kit: motile/tracksdata/pyscipopt/ilpy (or trackastra) offline wheels
description: Add ILP + tracking deps to local env (uv) and to the Kaggle kit dataset as offline wheels (internet off in kernel). tracksdata, geff, pyscipopt, ilpy, rustworkx OR trackastra. Verify import offline. Blocks 02x.

title: Post-proc GraphTransform chain: gap-close, short-track filter, linefit smooth, safe-divisions
description: Composable graph transforms (Protocol) applied in sequence to a linked TrackGraph. close_single_frame_gaps (reuse isolated node within ~3um else synth midpoint), filter_short_track_components (drop <7 unless division), linefit_smooth (topology-preserving coord smoothing w~0.8), add_safe_divisions (2nd child within ~4.5um). Each scored for marginal gain on fold 0. Enables best-of-each assembly. Blocks 02x.

title: Trackastra pretrained linker (offline) — evaluate vs ILP
description: Trackastra = pretrained transformer linker, division-aware, ships weights, runs offline, greedy or ILP mode. Wrap as Linker strategy; score on fold 0 vs motile-ILP and motion-Hungarian. Pick winner for the Frankenstein. Blocks 02x.

title: GPU-optimize detector kernel: LoG on CUDA, batch frames, enable_gpu
description: Kernel runtime ~12min, dominated by scipy gaussian_laplace (CPU, per-frame). NMS already torch.max_pool3d. Move LoG to torch conv3d on GPU (separable Gaussian + Laplacian), batch frames, set enable_gpu=true in kernel-metadata. Also profile local run on RTX 5090. Expect 12min -> ~1-2min. Owner note: 'should be faster on this machine if optimized well, and on gpu'.

title: Matched end-to-end score: best detector + division-aware linker at op point 1.0
description: Combine the pieces built this session: learned detector (3ws) OR classical, + DivisionAwareLinker (cdo, 7um gate) instead of NN, scored end-to-end at N_pred/N_total=1.0 (sct operating point) on the SAME held-out fold-0 videos, per prefix. This is the honest 'does the whole stack beat the classical floor' number and the local proxy for the leaderboard. Extends celltrack.operating_point to accept the division-aware linker. DONE WHEN: a matched classical-vs-learned end-to-end score table is in an interpretations/ note with the winner named.

title: Detector consistency objective — convert recall win into score
description: The matched A/B (interpretations/tracking/2026-07-23_operating-point-sweep.md) proved the learned detector wins recall (3ws) but LOSES end-to-end score vs the classical floor, because its centres jitter frame-to-frame and NN/division linking makes worse edges. Root-cause fix: add a temporal-consistency term to detection training (e.g. penalise centre displacement of the same cell across the window, or a warp-consistency loss) OR post-hoc centre smoothing. DONE WHEN: learned detector + division-aware linker beats the classical floor end-to-end at operating point 1.0 on the held-out fold, on the same videos.

title: Kaggle notebook-submission kernel (code competition)
description:
SETTLED in wy1: this is a Kaggle CODE competition — file upload via API 400s even for the official sample_submission.csv with rules accepted. Submission must be a notebook/script kernel run against the hidden test set, with a runtime cap.

Build a script kernel (.py, not .ipynb — honours the no-notebook rule) that: reads the mounted test .zarr under /kaggle/input, runs the pipeline, writes /kaggle/working/submission.csv in the exact scored format (proven in wy1). Node budget can't read train GEFFs on Kaggle — bake the per-prefix means as documented constants (44b6~36887, 6bba~16454) or estimate on-image.

Package celltrack+core as a Kaggle utility dataset and import it (DRY) rather than inlining. Push via kaggle kernels push, submit, read the LB score, reconcile against local. This is the reusable path every model submission uses — do it once here with the classical baseline to de-risk, reuse for 3ws/cdo.

DONE WHEN: the classical kernel submits successfully and returns a public LB score, reconciled against our local floor within a stated tolerance or explained.

title: End-to-end submission path, verified against the leaderboard
description:
Take the classical baseline through the whole path: predict on test -> submission CSV -> Kaggle
submit -> compare the returned public score against our local evaluator on the same predictions.

DONE WHEN: local and leaderboard scores agree within a stated tolerance, or the discrepancy is
explained. This is the only thing that proves our evaluator, our CSV convention and our
understanding of the hidden split are all correct - and it is far cheaper to discover a mismatch now
than after a trained model.

OPEN: whether this is a code competition with a runtime cap is still unverified (the API scope we
have does not expose the rules). Settle it here.

title: Grouped CV split by acquisition prefix
description:
44b6 (71 videos, 36.9k cells, 0.99% annotated) and 6bba (128 videos, 16.5k cells, 9.0% annotated) are
different acquisitions. A random split leaks acquisition identity and will read as generalisation.

Build the split in core/: grouped by prefix, with a held-out local validation set that is never
trained on. Report per-prefix scores separately as well as pooled - the pooled number hides which
acquisition a method actually helps.

DONE WHEN: the split is deterministic, committed as code (not a file of ids), and the two prefixes'
video counts and annotation totals are asserted in a test.
close_reason: Built as stratified-by-prefix at video level, not prefix-disjoint: the test split is 2 videos of each prefix, so holding an acquisition out would measure a harder task than the leaderboard. Per-prefix reporting kept. Dataset facts asserted in tests/e2e.

title: Bracket the score: linking-only ceiling and classical detector floor
description:
Two cheap runs that bound the problem before any model is trained.

(a) CEILING: link the GROUND-TRUTH nodes with nearest-neighbour matching between consecutive
timepoints. No detection error at all, so whatever this scores is the ceiling of a
nearest-neighbour linker - expected near 0.98 given that 2.1% of true links exceed 7 um.

(b) FLOOR: a classical detector (LoG/DoG on the quantile-normalised volume, anisotropy-aware sigma)
plus the same linker, scored end to end.

DONE WHEN: both numbers are in an interpretations/ note with the gap between them named. That gap is
the budget the learned detector has to win, and it decides whether effort goes into detection or
linking.
close_reason: Ceiling (NN linking of GT nodes) 0.998 edge Jaccard; floor (classical LoG detector + same linker) 0.5545 edge Jaccard / 0.5636 score, under-detecting to 37% of estimate. Gap ~0.44 is essentially all detection. Reproduced exactly on refactored code. See interpretations/tracking/2026-07-23_bracket.md.

title: Local evaluator matching the official metric
description:
Implement the competition metric in core/: bipartite node matching on centroid distance with a 7 um
cutoff in MICROMETRE space (anisotropic: 4.31 vox in z, 17.23 in y/x), edge TP/FP/FN with the rule
that unmatched predicted nodes generate no FP, adjusted edge jaccard against the GEFF
estimated_number_of_nodes, and the division jaccard over local fork windows.

DONE WHEN: our score agrees with the organizers' tracking_cellmot on the same (pred, gt) pairs to
within float noise, on at least one perfect-prediction case, one empty-prediction case and one
perturbed case. Their package is the oracle for the test, not a runtime dependency.

subsequent keep/kill decision noise.

title: [epic] GOAL: Epic 1 - architecture + first scored baseline
description:
Two strands, deliberately split. The BASELINE strand exists to produce a real leaderboard number
fast, using methods we already trust; the ARCHITECTURE strand builds the model that is meant to beat
it. They meet at the operating-point sweep.

The gate between them: nothing in the architecture strand is worth tuning until the evaluator is
verified and a trivial baseline has a number. Deadline 2026-09-29; top LB 0.929 as of 2026-07-23.

Score = adj_edge_jaccard + 0.1 * division_jaccard, with
adj_edge_jaccard = max(0, J * (1 - 0.1 * (N_pred - N_total)/N_total)).
See docs/PLAN.md and interpretations/tracking/2026-07-23_dataset-survey.md.

title: Random-rectangle crop augmentation (input regularization, stride-aligned)
description: Vary crop position AND size (currently fixed (16,64,64)+jitter) so the detector cannot memorize a fixed framing = input regularization. Sizes must be stride-aligned (z%2, y%8, x%8). Batching needs same-size-per-batch (bucket by size or pad). Test vs fixed-crop baseline.

title: Tiled inference (stitch prob map, peak globally) + stride-aligned crops
description: IF a frame stops fitting VRAM (does not at w64), spatial-tile: forward cubes with halo overlap >= receptive field, write each into a full-frame probability volume (average overlaps), then NMS/peak-pick ONCE on the global map. Boundary cells detected once, in global coords; tracking is already global so unaffected. Crops/tiles MUST be stride-aligned (z%2, y%8, x%8 for strides ((1,2,2),(1,2,2),(2,2,2))).

title: Explicit 80/10/10 train/val/test split (drop fold framing)
description: Replace the single fold-0 80/20 with an explicit 3-way train/val/test partition, stratified by prefix, deterministic by filename hash. Train=random-crop pool, val=per-epoch crop metric, test=final full-pipeline tracking-score (one test script). User is fine with 80/10/10 (or 90/10); no k-fold CV.
design: test=2/prefix (4 total, mirrors competition test size, LB-predictive), val=1/prefix (2 total, both acquisitions so metric means something), train=rest (~193). Deterministic by blake2b(filename) rank — same split every run, no seed. Per-epoch val = crop metric (fast); test = full tracking-score at end.
close_reason: StratifiedSplit committed e2168c0

title: Per-epoch checkpoint save + mlflow resume/continue-from-checkpoint
description: Save model checkpoint each epoch (mlflow artifact + weights file); support resume/continue training from a checkpoint. Enables warm-start and interrupt-resume. Note: warm-start is only valid when input distribution is unchanged (per CLAUDE.md) — a background-crops or objective change should train fresh.

title: Operating-point sweep: N_pred/N_total against realised score
description:
The adjustment ratio is signed and uncapped above, so predicting FEWER nodes than the estimated true
count multiplies the jaccard by more than 1 (up to 1.1). Detecting every cell earns exactly 1.0.

That argument is arithmetic on the formula, not an experiment. Sweep the detector's threshold across
N_pred/N_total and measure the realised score, per prefix - the aggregation weights each video by
its own TP+FP+FN, so the bonus is worth most where annotation is densest (6bba), which is also where
N_total is smallest and the ratio moves fastest.

DONE WHEN: the sweep curve is in an interpretations/ note with the chosen operating point and the
reason, including whether the bonus survives the edge FNs that under-detection causes.
close_reason: Sweep DONE-WHEN met with learned detector + NN linker: curve recorded, operating point ~1.0, under-detection (0.5x) collapses score (0.24/0.30) so the node-count bonus does NOT survive edge FNs. Force-closed past the cdo dependency — the curve stands for the current pipeline; re-running with the learned linker after cdo is a refinement. Surfaced: learned recall beats classical but end-to-end score (~0.45-0.48) < classical floor (~0.56); recall != score. See interpretations/tracking/2026-07-23_operating-point-sweep.md.

title: Detection model: 3D U-Net with temporal context
description:
Per-voxel detection map over an anisotropic volume, cell centres recovered by local-maximum
suppression with an NMS radius derived from the physics (voxel spacing + measured cell scale), not
tuned by hand.

Anisotropy is 4x: an isotropic kernel in index space is an ellipsoid in the tissue. Either use
anisotropic kernels/strides or resample - decide with an argument, and record it.

DONE WHEN: detection recall against the annotated nodes beats the classical detector from the
bracket task at a matched node count, on the held-out prefix split.
close_reason: Learned anisotropy-aware 3D U-Net beats the classical floor's recall at matched node count on held-out fold 0, both prefixes: 44b6 0.656->0.766, 6bba 0.664->0.742. Trained 40 videos/2000 steps, masked MSE 0.040->0.006, no tuning. Single-run/2-videos-per-prefix; direction credible (both acquisitions agree). See interpretations/tracking/2026-07-23_detection-beats-floor.md.

title: Linking model: candidate generation plus learned scoring
description:
Candidates are generated with a radius that covers the measured motion tail (median 1.82 um/frame,
p99 8.38, max 60.8) - deliberately WIDER than the 7 um matching cutoff, so the scorer has real
competitors to discriminate rather than a single obvious partner. Then a learned pairwise score over
consecutive frames, resolved into a one-to-one assignment (plus the two-child case at divisions).

DONE WHEN: it beats nearest-neighbour linking on ground-truth nodes - i.e. it exceeds the ceiling
from the bracket task, which is exactly the number nearest-neighbour cannot pass.
close_reason: Division-aware linker beats NN on GT nodes: edge Jaccard 0.9980 > 0.9976, and decisively on full score 1.1222 > 1.0884 via the division term (NN div_jaccard=0, structural; division-aware 0.333). Composes NN one-to-one then attaches unmatched daughters to nearest matched parent within a tight 7um division radius (=matching cutoff; wider gates add false divisions). Exceeds the bracket ceiling = DONE-WHEN. Note: real score bottleneck is detection jitter, not GT-node linking (see operating-point-sweep). See interpretations/tracking/2026-07-23_division-linking.md.

title: Training harness: crop sampling, masked supervision, tracking
description:
The data loader and run scaffolding both models sit on. Samples (T, Z, Y, X) crops from the zarr
stores (one timepoint per chunk, so temporal windows are the natural read unit), applies the
quantile normalisation the stores ship, and carries the annotation mask.

The masked supervision is the load-bearing part: ground truth is hand-followed lineages covering
~6% of cells, so an unlabelled bright blob is a real cell, not background. Unlabelled positives must
be excluded from the loss rather than scored as negatives.

DONE WHEN: a smoke run trains for a few hundred steps on a handful of videos, logs to MLflow, and
the mask demonstrably zeroes the gradient on unannotated regions (asserted in a test).
close_reason: Training harness complete: CropSampler + DetectionTarget (masked supervision: positive near centres, negative in dark tissue, EXCLUDED for bright-unlabelled) + MaskedDetectionLoss + DetectionUNet + DetectionTrainer. DONE-WHEN met: smoke run 300 steps/4 real videos on GPU, loss 0.052->0.004, logged to MLflow; mask-zeroes-gradient pinned in a unit test. 14 tests, gates green.

title: Evaluate Rust file-loading backend (PyO3) for crop extraction
description: Fuse decompress+crop+normalize+augment in native Rust off the GIL, returning ready crops to the DataLoader. Would maximize throughput. BUT: likely UNNECESSARY - the bottleneck is the 32x over-read, which re-chunk (6v0) fixes cheaply with no new tech; blosc decompress is already C. Revisit ONLY if still data-bound after re-chunk + 16 workers. Higher effort (Rust toolchain, PyO3 bindings, zarr-rust or manual blosc). P3 fallback.
close_reason: moot: after rechunk the loop is compute-bound (GPU 86-96%), not IO-bound. RAM-cache/Rust would speed data the GPU already can't consume faster.

title: RAM LRU frame cache in CellVideo (alternative to re-chunk)
description: Frames are 8MB, RAM=94GB. An LRU cache in CellVideo.frame() could hold ~thousands of decompressed frames. CAVEAT: DataLoader workers are separate processes (Windows spawn) so each caches independently -> duplication + only partial hit-rate on random anchors across 158 videos. Re-chunk (6v0) is cleaner (per-read fix, no duplication). Only pursue if re-chunk is blocked. P3.
close_reason: moot: after rechunk the loop is compute-bound (GPU 86-96%), not IO-bound. RAM-cache/Rust would speed data the GPU already can't consume faster.
